leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members prefer optical lattice clocks (B012) as a single-part prize to Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye. All five give the same two names and a citation built on the invention and development of the optical lattice clock (magic-wavelength trapping, uncertainty near 1e-18); they describe the result as quantitative and independently reproduced and compared across laboratories. They also share the same reservations: possible overlap with the 2005 (Hall, Haensch) and 2012 (Wineland, Haroche) prizes, early-developer claims outside the pair (Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Pal'chikov), and the pending redefinition of the second. Citation wording differs: Johansson and Pearce emphasise the 10^-18 level, Kroll and Olsson a new regime of precision measurement, Lindroth the magic wavelength. Danielsson (who ranked it second) and Eriksson, who prefer B042, list it as an alternative; Johansson moved to it from circuit QED after reading the openings, and Pearce moved it from fourth place.

Three of eight members prefer magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B042) as a single-part prize to Allan H. MacDonald, Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and Rafi Bistritzer. All three describe a theory-then-experiment sequence (continuum-model prediction of flat bands, then correlated insulating and superconducting states) and a large independent follow-up literature. Eriksson and Mehlig add moire quantum materials to the citation; Danielsson's wording stays closer to the two findings. The three supporters also volunteer the same weaknesses: the superconducting mechanism is still debated, twist-angle disorder limits reproducibility, and Yuan Cao, Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and the Dean, Young, Yacoby and Efetov groups fall outside the trio. Each of the three names B012 as an alternative, and each says the optical lattice clock would be a more mature choice or an acceptable one. B042 is in turn an alternative for Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce, who prefer B012.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 configurations are single-part prizes with one ballot ID; no member proposes a combination of two ballots, and Mehlig explicitly notes the three-person limit makes a two-achievement prize impractical.
The laureate sets within each of B012 (Katori, Ye) and B042 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) are identical across all members who prefer them.

Each of the three B042 supporters names B012 as an alternative, and four of the five B012 supporters (all except Johansson) name B042 as an alternative, so the choice is mainly between two ballots rather than a spread of many.

Several members who prefer other candidates shifted after reading the openings: Johansson from circuit QED (B005) to B012, and Pearce from IceCube (B035) to B012; Pearce now holds B035 only as an alternative.

Independent reproduction is the common test: B012 is cited as reproduced and compared at the 1e-18 level by JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and NPL, and B042 as reproduced by several independent moire groups.
Both leading candidates are accepted as original and consequential; the disagreement is about maturity, credit and prize history, not whether the physics is real.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a distinct achievement or an incremental extension of precision-metrology work already recognised in 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (control of single quantum systems, including ion clocks). Supporters of B012 call the magic-wavelength lattice a distinct invention; they also record the overlap as their strongest reservation.

Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and the debated nature of the correlated insulators in twisted bilayer graphene are part of the discovery that must be settled, or are open follow-up questions. B042 supporters treat them as follow-up; Pearce and the B012 supporters treat them as a maturity concern.
Whether the experimental claim for B042 is sufficiently robust given twist-angle disorder and sample-to-sample variation, as flagged by Eriksson and Mehlig.

Whether the astroparticle candidates (B035 IceCube, B016 GRB afterglows) can be assessed fairly by a committee in which only the Chair and Danielsson rank them; Danielsson ranks B035 seventh because the sources of the diffuse flux are unidentified.
attribution_disputes: B012: Lemonde, Pal'chikov, Takamoto and Ludlow, and ion-clock groups, are named by several members as having early lattice-clock claims outside the pair Katori and Ye. Pearce asks whether Ye's contribution is central to the citation; Kroll asks whether the first lattice-clock demonstrations and the many-body clock work should be described separately.

B042: Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 experiments, is outside the three credited names. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto (earlier continuum model) and the Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov and Yazdani groups (follow-ups) are also raised. Mehlig asks whether a split of two theory names and one experimental name is the right allocation.

Where B012 and B042 look comparable as clean, three-or-fewer-name prizes, they differ in how clean the credit is: B012 has two names on which all six members who ranked it agree, whereas B042 has three names that raise the question of how much of the experimental credit is covered by a single experimental laureate.

B035 is credited to Francis Halzen alone, and Pearce and Danielsson both question whether one name is defensible for an IceCube collaboration of hundreds. B016 (Costa, Frontera, Kulkarni) leaves out the optical and radio followers, as Danielsson notes.
maturity_disputes: B012 is considered mature by its supporters, with independent comparisons at the 1e-18 level. Several members note the SI second has not yet been redefined and ask whether the committee should wait for that, or treat it as a consequence of the discovery rather than a precondition.

B042 is about eight years after the 2018 experiments. Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig accept this as sufficient but each concedes that the field is young and that B012 is the safer, more mature choice; Lindroth asks whether the pairing mechanism needs to be settled before the topic ceases to count as premature.

B005 (circuit QED) follows the 2025 prize on superconducting-circuit macroscopic quantum tunnelling by one year; Johansson and Pearce raise a possible imbalance, and Eriksson, who chaired for 2025, says he considered the overlap.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: director of WACQT (Chalmers) and professionally active in circuit QED; flags possible recusal or discounting on B005, and to a lesser extent B020 and B019. No conflict is disclosed for B012.
Kroll: leads part of WACQT, which overlaps institutionally with Johansson's home; he defers to Johansson on B005, which is not in his preferred configuration. No tie to Katori or Ye.

Pearce (Chair): collaboration membership in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, and gamma-ray polarimetry plans, put him in the same field as B035 and B016. He would consider stepping back from a decision on either if it became the leading candidate; neither is the preferred configuration of any member.
Lindroth: long-standing collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate); no shortlisted ballot credits her. Her field is close to B012, B019 and B020 and she asks colleagues to test her view.

Eriksson: chaired the committee for the 2025 prize on superconducting-circuit tunnelling and has taken the overlap with B005 into account. Olsson notes a Chalmers colleague relation with Johansson and no tie to any credited name. Danielsson and Mehlig disclose no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B012: is the committee satisfied that a citation naming the magic-wavelength lattice and its realisation separates the work from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and if not, what wording or what omission would make the overlap objection decisive?

For B012: do Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow or other early lattice-clock groups have a priority claim strong enough to displace or add to Katori and Ye, and are Ye's contributions (strontium clock, many-body clock, frequency-comb link) central enough to justify his place? Lindroth and Kroll, please state this plainly.

For B042: is the superconducting mechanism part of the discovery to be rewarded, or a follow-up question, and how would the committee handle Yuan Cao, Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto if only three may be named?
Is the redefinition of the second a precondition for awarding B012, or a consequence the committee need not wait for? Please give a reason, not only a preference.

Are the B042 supporters (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig) willing to rank B012 above B042 on maturity grounds, and are the B012 supporters willing to say what additional evidence on B042 would move them? Each of the three supporters already names B012 as an alternative.

Should B035, B016 or B005 remain in the discussion at all, given that no member prefers them in round 1 and Johansson and Pearce have flagged timing or conflict issues? If a member wants any of them kept, which specific point is unresolved?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a five-to-three split between two single-ballot configurations, B012 (Katori, Ye) and B042 (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer), with seven of eight members naming the other as an alternative (Johansson alone does not). The split follows less a difference over whether the physics is real than over maturity, attribution and the weight of prior metrology prizes. The five-member count for B012 is a count of explicit round-1 positions only, and it includes my own, which moved after reading the openings; it is not a ruling and no vote is implied. B012's open questions concern novelty and early-developer credit. B042's open questions concern the superconducting mechanism and the experimental credit. Round 2 should address these specific points.
